issue_context.title: Implement GUID map
issue_context.body:
##### Summary

Implement a global (across hosts) lookup structure that will 

- Map UUIDs (128 bit) to objects (hosts/charts/dimensions) as defined in the [design](https://github.com/netdata/docs/blob/master/architecture/agent/db/database-log-format-pros-cons.md).

- Map unique name identifiers (e.g. concatenated ids of host|chart|dimension) of objects to UUIDs (128 bit) Ref: [here](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/8183)

Find suitable hash map library. Consider:
- Judy
- Sparsehash
- Android libcutils/hashmap
- khash
- AVL?

or something else.

We decided to use Judy + AVL to reuse existing libraries.
Risk: High memory and CPU overheads.

review_comments: This will crash if Judy returns an error condition. For example if `uuid==0` then it will trigger an internal error inside `JudyLIns` which returns `~0`. Always dereferencing seems dangerous - should this be `if (PValue!=PPJERR && *PValue)` ?

Currently netdata always crashes when out of memory like in:
https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/98c7260d929a2f6ad2aabb4b27f0d77d49f6cae8/libnetdata/libnetdata.c#L86

We are consistently crashing in dbengine as well, but we're not logging it similarly.
If we are to be consistent we could add:
```
    if (PPJERR==PValue) fatal("JudyHSIns() cannot allocate memory.");
```

This would cover the out of memory case, but there are multiple conditions in Judy that trigger that error return. The other one that I saw in the review was parameter error. In this case we could guard against the parameter error explicitly, or guard against the error being returned from Judy. I think guarding against the error returning from Judy is overall more robust.
